note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason: cinatra#3002 (PR 3197), the forward merge of origin/main into the branch, so `from` is main's OWN committed ceiling at ba0ce2e4b0afa338596805592fa9e374d40efce7 and the whole raise is this branch's. TWO leaves, and no other module: (1) packages/agents/src/run-final-response-receipt.ts, the fix leg 2 receipt imported statically by packages/agents/src/execution.ts and called on the terminal-completion transition that file owns, reachable through the run-completion spine all four routes already reach; (2) src/components/ui/status-pill.tsx, which the fix leg 3 run-detail headers now import in place of the generic badge, because the ratified drawing draws that header as the design system's status pill rather than a badge. The branch adds no other first-party module to any tracked graph: its other new files are tests, which the analyzer does not walk. Neither leaf is reachable from /sign-in, whose ceiling and carried-forward record this merge leaves exactly as main committed them. MEASURED, NOT COMPUTED, and not hand-merged: with the companion extension fleet cloned PINNED exactly as CI clones it (116/116, missingCount 0 on every route) THREE trees were analysed in ONE environment by the same scripts/route-graph.mjs. origin/main alone lands EXACTLY on its four committed ceilings (/api/mcp 1764, /chat 1867, /api/a2a 1772, /api/llm-bridge 1782). The merge measures /api/mcp 1766, /chat 1868, /api/a2a 1774, /api/llm-bridge 1784. The third tree is the merge with the status-pill import edge removed and nothing else changed, and it measures /api/mcp 1765, /chat 1868, /api/a2a 1773, /api/llm-bridge 1783 — which isolates the two leaves per route: the receipt is +1 on all four, and the status pill is +1 on /api/mcp, /api/a2a and /api/llm-bridge and +0 on /chat, which already reached that module by another edge. That is exactly the +2/+1/+2/+2 committed here, so nothing of main's is folded into this branch's raise. /sign-in measures 163 on all three trees, far under its 223 ceiling, which is therefore carried forward UNEDITED: a route this branch does not touch is neither raised nor ratcheted down by this merge. Narrowing is unavailable for either leaf. scripts/route-graph.mjs extractSpecifiers counts a dynamic import() specifier as exactly the same first-party graph pressure as a static one (the metric is static reachability by design, not runtime bundle inclusion), so making either edge lazy would not lower the measured count; the receipt must be written synchronously on the terminal-completion transition inside execution.ts, the one place the run's final response is known; and the status pill is a shared design-system component that both run-detail headers must resolve to ONE of, so it can neither be duplicated per host nor split behind a route-specific entry point. The PR 3048 records this raise supersedes on all four routes are RETIRED BY IT, the one lifecycle the gate allows for an annotation whose ceiling moves.
